questions.question: What is the main purpose of Configuration Management in a complex project, like building a robot or a detailed computer program?

options.A: To make sure the project is finished as quickly as possible, even if some details are missed.
options.B: To keep track of all the parts, plans, and changes so everyone on the team always works with the correct and latest versions.
options.C: To decide which team member gets to build the most important or difficult parts of the project.
options.D: To only focus on the final testing phase, ignoring how the project was put together.

questions.explanation: Configuration Management is about maintaining order, understanding what you have, and carefully managing any changes throughout your project's lifecycle, ensuring your creation remains coherent and functional.

questions.question: In Creationeering, what does a 'baseline' represent in a project?

options.A: The very first rough sketch or idea you have for your project.
options.B: A list of all the tools and materials you will need to begin building.
options.C: A formally agreed-upon snapshot of your project's design or configuration at a specific point in time, used as a trusted reference.
options.D: The final step of verifying that your completed creation works perfectly.

questions.explanation: A baseline is a formally agreed-upon snapshot of a system's configuration at a specific point in time, serving as a reference point for future changes and development.

questions.question: Why is 'Change Control' an essential part of Configuration Management for maintaining a system's integrity?

options.A: It allows anyone on the team to make changes to the design whenever they think it's a good idea.
options.B: It ensures that all requests for changes are carefully evaluated, approved, tracked, and implemented in an organized way.
options.C: It helps the team remember the initial goals of the project before any work begins.
options.D: It is only necessary for very small and simple projects where few changes are expected.

questions.explanation: Change Control is the process of managing all requests for changes to a system's configuration, including evaluating, approving, tracking, and implementing those changes in a structured way to maintain integrity.

questions.question: How does God's creation in Genesis 1 connect to the concept of establishing baselines in our Creationeering projects?

options.A: God created everything randomly, showing that strict baselines are not always needed for creation.
options.B: God established a clear, ordered, and functional state for each phase of creation, declaring it 'good,' which served as a stable baseline for the next step.
options.C: God's creation was so perfect that He didn't need to manage any changes or configurations after the initial act.
options.D: The Bible only talks about creation, not about managing ongoing projects or changes.

questions.explanation: The lesson explains that God's declaration of 'good' after each phase of creation signifies a completed, stable, and acceptable configuration for that stage, acting as a baseline for the next step.

questions.question: In the Creationeering framework, why is Configuration Management especially important during the 'Assembly phase' of a project?

options.A: Because the Assembly phase is when you decide on the very first design ideas and requirements.
options.B: Because once parts start coming together, many changes can happen, and it's easy for things to get messy without careful tracking and management.
options.C: Because Configuration Management is only about verifying and validating the design before any building starts.
options.D: Because it's the only time you need to think about what specific tools and equipment you'll use.

questions.explanation: The lesson states that Configuration Management fits the Assembly phase because 'once parts start coming together, things can get messy fast,' and a small change to one piece can affect many others, requiring careful tracking.
